subject: math
description: Students graph functions expressed symbolically and identify the key features of each graph, working by hand for simple cases. For Algebra 2 the families extend beyond the Algebra 1 set to the ones this standard adds at this level: higher-degree polynomial functions (showing zeros, multiplicity, end behavior, and turning points), exponential functions $f(x)=a\,b^{x}+k$ (showing the $y$-intercept, horizontal asymptote, growth or decay, and end behavior), logarithmic functions $f(x)=a\log_b(x-h)+k$ (showing the vertical asymptote, $x$-intercept, and domain), rational functions $f(x)=\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$ (showing vertical and horizontal asymptotes, holes, and intercepts), and trigonometric functions $f(x)=a\sin(b(x-c))+d$ and its cosine and tangent analogues (showing amplitude, period, phase shift, midline, and asymptotes). For each family students locate and label the defining key features, plot points or anchor features to sketch the graph, read features off a given graph, match a symbolic rule to its graph, and recover a parameter from a labeled feature.
subSkills: Graph a polynomial in factored form $f(x)=a(x-r_1)(x-r_2)\cdots$ and identify the zeros, their multiplicities (cross vs. touch), the $y$-intercept, and the end behavior from the leading term
Determine the end behavior of a polynomial from the sign of the leading coefficient and the parity of the degree
Graph an exponential function $f(x)=a\,b^{x}+k$ and identify the $y$-intercept, the horizontal asymptote $y=k$, whether it grows or decays, and the end behavior
Graph a logarithmic function $f(x)=a\log_b(x-h)+k$ and identify the vertical asymptote $x=h$, the $x$-intercept, and the domain $x>h$
Graph a rational function and identify vertical asymptotes (from zeros of the denominator), the horizontal or slant asymptote (from degree comparison), holes (common factors), and intercepts
Graph a sine or cosine function $f(x)=a\sin(b(x-c))+d$ and identify amplitude $|a|$, period $\frac{2\pi}{|b|}$, phase shift $c$, and midline $y=d$
Graph a tangent function and identify its period $\frac{\pi}{|b|}$ and the locations of its vertical asymptotes
Read key features (asymptotes, intercepts, amplitude, period, zeros) off a given graph and state them exactly
Match a symbolic rule to the correct graph using its key features, and recover a parameter such as $a$, $b$, $h$, $k$, $c$, or $d$ from a labeled feature

problemArchetypes.name: Polynomial in factored form (zeros, multiplicity, end behavior)
problemArchetypes.example: Graph $f(x)=(x+2)(x-1)^2$. Give the zeros with their behavior, the $y$-intercept, and the end behavior. Zeros: $x=-2$ (crosses), $x=1$ (touches, multiplicity $2$); $y$-intercept $(0,2)$; as $x\to-\infty,\,f\to-\infty$ and as $x\to\infty,\,f\to\infty$.

problemArchetypes.name: Exponential function (intercept, asymptote, growth/decay)
problemArchetypes.example: Graph $f(x)=2\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x}+1$. Give the $y$-intercept, horizontal asymptote, and whether it grows or decays. $y$-intercept $(0,3)$; asymptote $y=1$; decays toward $y=1$ as $x\to\infty$.

problemArchetypes.name: Logarithmic function (asymptote, intercept, domain)
problemArchetypes.example: Graph $f(x)=\log_2(x-1)$. Give the vertical asymptote, the $x$-intercept, and the domain. Asymptote $x=1$; $x$-intercept $(2,0)$; domain $x>1$.

problemArchetypes.name: Rational function (asymptotes, holes, intercepts)
problemArchetypes.example: Graph $f(x)=\frac{x-3}{x^2-9}$. Give all asymptotes, any hole, and the intercepts. Hole at $x=3$; vertical asymptote $x=-3$; horizontal asymptote $y=0$; $y$-intercept $\left(0,\tfrac{1}{3}\right)$.

problemArchetypes.name: Sine or cosine function (amplitude, period, phase shift, midline)
problemArchetypes.example: Graph $f(x)=3\sin\!\left(2\left(x-\tfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)+1$. Give amplitude, period, phase shift, and midline. Amplitude $3$; period $\pi$; phase shift $\frac{\pi}{4}$ right; midline $y=1$.

problemArchetypes.name: Tangent function (period, asymptotes)
problemArchetypes.example: Graph $f(x)=\tan(2x)$. Give the period and two consecutive vertical asymptotes. Period $\frac{\pi}{2}$; asymptotes at $x=\frac{\pi}{4}$ and $x=-\frac{\pi}{4}$.

problemArchetypes.name: Read features off a given graph
problemArchetypes.example: An exponential graph passes through $(0,5)$ and flattens toward $y=1$ as $x\to\infty$. Give its horizontal asymptote and state whether it grows or decays. Asymptote $y=1$; it decays.

problemArchetypes.name: Match rule to graph / recover a parameter
problemArchetypes.example: A sinusoid has amplitude $4$, midline $y=-2$, and period $4\pi$. Write an equation of the form $f(x)=a\sin(bx)+d$. Answer: $f(x)=4\sin\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}x\right)-2$.

Easy.description: A single family in its most direct form, with key features readable from the symbolic rule or anchor points with little or no computation. Graph a parent or one-shift exponential and name its asymptote and $y$-intercept, read the amplitude and midline off $f(x)=a\sin(bx)+d$, name the zeros of a polynomial already in factored form, or read one obvious feature off a supplied graph. One representation, one or two features. tier1 begins here.
constraints: Exponential $f(x)=a\,b^{x}+k$ with integer $a,k$ and base $b=2,3,\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{3}$; ask for the $y$-intercept and asymptote
Logarithm $f(x)=\log_b(x-h)$ with integer $h$ and no vertical stretch; ask for the asymptote or domain
Polynomial given fully factored with distinct integer zeros and $a=\pm1$; ask for the zeros and the $y$-intercept
Sine or cosine of the form $f(x)=a\sin(bx)+d$ with no phase shift; ask for amplitude, period, and midline only
At most two features, each read directly from the rule or graph

Medium.description: Requires a short computation or accounting for one extra transformation before the features appear, or a less direct family. Determine end behavior and multiplicity behavior of a polynomial, compute the period from $b$ and locate the phase shift of a sinusoid, find the asymptotes of a logarithm with a vertical stretch, or find the vertical and horizontal asymptotes and intercepts of a rational function with no hole. Two to three features per item. tier1 ends here; tier2 begins here.
constraints: Polynomial in factored form with a repeated factor; report multiplicity behavior (cross vs. touch) and end behavior together
Sinusoid $f(x)=a\sin(b(x-c))+d$ with a genuine phase shift; report amplitude, period $\frac{2\pi}{|b|}$, phase shift, and midline
Logarithm $f(x)=a\log_b(x-h)+k$ with a stretch and a vertical shift; find the asymptote, domain, and $x$-intercept
Rational function with degree of numerator less than or equal to degree of denominator, no common factor; find vertical and horizontal asymptotes and the intercepts
Match a symbolic rule to one of several graphs using two distinguishing features

Hard.description: Multi-step or multi-feature reasoning within a more demanding family, or recovering a parameter from features. Graph a rational function with a hole and a slant asymptote, build a full key-feature description of a polynomial or sinusoid, recover a parameter ($a$, $b$, $h$, $k$, $c$, or $d$) from a labeled feature, or graph a tangent and locate its asymptotes. Three or more linked features, or a parameter that must be solved for. tier2 lives here.
constraints: Rational function with a common factor (a hole) and either a slant asymptote (numerator degree one more than denominator) or competing leading coefficients for the horizontal asymptote
Recover a parameter from a feature, e.g. find $b$ from a stated period, find $a$ from a point and a midline, or write a log/exponential equation from a labeled asymptote and intercept
Full key-feature description: for a polynomial give all zeros with multiplicity, the $y$-intercept, and the end behavior; for a sinusoid give amplitude, period, phase shift, and midline together
Tangent or cotangent function with $b\neq1$; give the period $\frac{\pi}{|b|}$ and at least two consecutive vertical asymptotes as exact multiples of $\pi$
Exact-value answers required (radicals, fractions, multiples of $\pi$), no rounded decimals

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student reverses the sign when reading the phase shift or horizontal translation from $(x-c)$ or $(x-h)$
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $f(x)=3\sin(2(x-\tfrac{\pi}{4}))$ reports a phase shift of $\frac{\pi}{4}$ left, or for $f(x)=\log_2(x-1)$ states the asymptote as $x=-1$ instead of $x=1$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student confuses amplitude with period or forgets to divide by $b$ when finding the period
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $f(x)=3\sin(2x)+1$ states the period as $2$ or $2\pi$ instead of $\frac{2\pi}{2}=\pi$, or reports the amplitude as $2$ (using $b$) instead of $3$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student treats the horizontal asymptote or midline as $y=0$, ignoring the vertical shift $k$ or $d$
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $f(x)=2\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x}+1$ gives the asymptote as $y=0$ and the $y$-intercept as $(0,2)$ instead of $y=1$ and $(0,3)$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student misreads polynomial end behavior, ignoring the sign of the leading coefficient or the parity of the degree
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $f(x)=(x+2)(x-1)^2$ (degree $3$, positive leading coefficient) claims both ends rise, as if it were even degree, instead of falling on the left and rising on the right

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student treats every zero as a crossing, ignoring even multiplicity where the graph only touches the axis
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $f(x)=(x+2)(x-1)^2$ says the graph crosses at $x=1$ instead of touching and turning there

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student finds a vertical asymptote at a value that is actually a hole, missing the cancelled common factor
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $f(x)=\frac{x-3}{x^2-9}$ reports vertical asymptotes at both $x=3$ and $x=-3$, instead of a hole at $x=3$ and a single asymptote at $x=-3$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student picks the wrong horizontal asymptote rule for a rational function, ignoring the degree comparison
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $f(x)=\frac{x-3}{x^2-9}$ (numerator degree less than denominator) gives the horizontal asymptote as $y=1$ instead of $y=0$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student swaps the domain and range relationship of exponential and logarithmic functions, giving the wrong domain or asymptote orientation
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $f(x)=\log_2(x-1)$ states the domain as all real numbers or gives a horizontal asymptote $y=1$, instead of domain $x>1$ with vertical asymptote $x=1$
